sections.title: Text becomes pieces before maths
paragraphs: A {{largeLanguageModel}} does not ingest a paragraph as one blob of Unicode. It splits text into {{token}}s: whole words, subwords or punctuation fragments.
Each {{token}} maps to an id. That id selects an {{embedding}} row. Only then do the weighted layers and {{attention}} blocks run.
Tokenization is inside the serving stack of the model family you call. Change tokenizer, change ids, change the path numbers take through the network.
Context limits are counted in {{token}}s, not characters. A short English sentence and a dense code snippet can cost very different budgets.
This lesson closes the foundation spine's look at how data enters the network. Next track work shifts toward outside behavior: instructions, answers and scoring.

check.prompt: Why can two strings with similar character length use different amounts of context budget?
check.answer: Tokenizers split text into different numbers of tokens
choices: Tokenizers split text into different numbers of tokens
check.explanation: Budgets are in {{token}}s. Different languages, code and punctuation produce different splits, so character length is a weak guide.

sections.title: Subwords and surprises
paragraphs: Modern tokenizers often use subwords so rare terms can be built from pieces. That keeps the vocabulary finite while still covering new spellings.
A space, a capital letter or a missing accent can change the {{token}} boundary. Tiny string edits sometimes create large id changes.
When you evaluate models later, keep prompts byte-identical if you want a fair outside comparison. Silent tokenizer differences across providers are a real footgun.
Click each example. Honesty: this hub will not ship a full byte-pair trainer. You need the mental model of pieces → ids → embeddings.
Inside perspective: fluent text is still discrete symbols to the network. That is one reason models can miss a character-level typo humans forgive instantly.

reveals.prompt: Word "unhappiness" might become un + happiness pieces.
reveals.reveal: Subwords let the model reuse parts it has seen even when the full word is rare.

reveals.prompt: Adding a leading space changes token ids.
reveals.reveal: Common gotcha. Identical-looking prompts may not be identical inside.

reveals.prompt: You compare two providers on the "same" prompt string.
reveals.reveal: Still verify behavior: different tokenizers mean different inside paths.

check.prompt: You paste the same customer question into two APIs and get odd gaps. What inside factor should you suspect first?
check.answer: Different tokenizers producing different token ids
choices: Different tokenizers producing different token ids
Softmax being illegal in both APIs
Decision trees running inside every LLM
Embeddings being stored as PNG files
check.explanation: Providers may tokenize differently. That changes ids and {{embedding}} lookups before any shared {{prompt}} wording can help.

sections.title: Hand-off to outside behavior
paragraphs: You can now sketch the inside path: text → {{token}}s → embeddings → layers → scores → (often) probabilities → generated {{token}}s.
The next track, LLM systems, focuses on the outside: how you instruct the model, how answers look and how you score them with evidence.
**Prompts as instructions** starts that outside craft. You will still benefit from knowing tokens and embeddings exist underneath every call.
Optional side paths (trees, rewards, GANs) remain available from earlier parents if you want other learning styles. They are not required for Continue.
Next lesson: **Prompts as instructions**. Carry the inside map with you when answers look magical.
bullets: Inside path ends at generated tokens.
Outside path begins with clear prompts.

check.prompt: In a short phrase, what is the first inside step when text hits a language model?
check.answer: Split text into tokens for embedding lookup
check.explanation: Before weighted layers run, text becomes {{token}} ids and those ids select {{embedding}} rows. That is the entry ramp inside the model.

recapQuestions.prompt: Context windows are usually measured in what unit?
recapQuestions.explanation: Limits and billing for {{largeLanguageModel}}s are tied to {{token}} counts, which depend on the tokenizer.

recapQuestions.prompt: Complete the inside entry path: text → tokens → …
recapQuestions.explanation: After tokenization, ids select {{embedding}}s and the network transforms those vectors. That is the core inside entry path.
